product: Payday loan, title loan, personal loan, or advance loan
issue: Can't stop withdrawals from your bank account

themes.label: Refusal to honor ACH revocation
themes.description: Consumers claim lenders refused, ignored, or conditioned requests to revoke ACH or electronic transfer authorization, sometimes citing outstanding balances or one-time transfer rules.

examples.summary: A consumer claims a payday lender continued to withdraw funds from their bank account after the consumer revoked authorization, refused to honor the revocation claiming the consumer owed money, and prevented the consumer from stopping the payments through their bank.

Consumer claims a lender repeatedly refused requests to revoke ACH authorization for an outstanding loan balance, stating the revocation could not be granted due to the outstanding balance, despite the consumer citing Regulation E rights.
Consumer claims lender refused to honor revocation of electronic fund transfer authorization and conditioned removal of ACH access on funding a new account to repay an outstanding balance.

themes.label: Debits continuing after revocation or cancellation
themes.description: Consumers claim withdrawals were still attempted or made after they revoked authorization, disabled autopay, or asked to discontinue, sometimes causing overdraft or bank fees.

examples.summary: Consumer claims that after revoking authorization for electronic fund transfers and having bank account information removed from the lender's system, the lender debited their account anyway, and the consumer was unable to reach the lender for resolution.
Consumer claims that after revoking ACH authorization, the lender attempted a withdrawal that caused a $36 overdraft fee despite the consumer's stated revocation request.
Consumer claims that after emailing the company to discontinue ACH withdrawals in accordance with the terms and conditions, the company attempted an ACH withdrawal anyway.

themes.label: Withdrawals after payoff or account closure
themes.description: Consumers claim funds continued to be taken after a loan was paid in full or an account was closed, with some alleging unresolved refunds or later collection efforts.

examples.summary: Consumer claims lender continued withdrawing funds from payroll after loan repayment was complete and failed to stop deductions despite multiple requests and refunds for overpayments.

Consumer claims continued unauthorized bank account withdrawals occurred after loan repayment was complete, and a refund of over $2,800 promised within 35 business days has not been issued despite months passing and supervisor follow-up never occurring.
Consumer claims that after repaying the full loan amount through multiple payments, the lender continued to withdraw funds from the consumer's bank account without authorization.

themes.label: Membership and subscription fee withdrawals
themes.description: Consumers claim recurring membership, subscription, or plan charges were withdrawn from their accounts and were hard to cancel or deactivate.

examples.summary: Consumer claims a lender charges membership fees that are withdrawn from the account before loan payments, leaving insufficient funds for loan repayment, and continues these withdrawals despite the consumer's request to stop.
Consumer claims lender continued to automatically debit monthly subscription fees from checking account after consumer revoked authorization and requested cancellation.

Consumer claims the lender made account plan upgrades sneakily with immediate charges, automatically reactivated the account with billing upon login, and made the deactivation process deliberately confusing with small-print options and misleading interface design.

themes.label: Unexplained or unconsented account debits
themes.description: Consumers claim withdrawals, account access, or balance offsets occurred without clear consent, notice, or explanation, including data access concerns.

examples.summary: Consumer claims multiple unauthorized withdrawals were debited from their account, that customer service was unable to explain the transactions despite being shown account statements, and that a similar issue occurred years prior with funds never returned.

Consumer claims that after requesting account deletion months earlier, the company continued monitoring their bank account without consent, failed to unlink bank account information from its system, and a suspicious text message containing sensitive account details was sent from an unknown number, raising concerns about either phishing or a data breach.

Consumer claims that incoming funds received through Cash App were automatically applied toward a loan balance without prior notice or consent, leaving the consumer unable to access money needed for basic living expenses during financial hardship.

brief.headline: Claims of unstoppable bank withdrawals on short-term loans are surging, concentrated in a few companies
brief.what_is_happening: Complaints that consumers cannot stop withdrawals from their bank accounts tied to payday, personal, and advance loans are accelerating. Velocity is 1.7683, ranked 1 of 79 clusters. The recent monthly average is 43.33 versus a baseline of 22.33, with a June 2026 peak of 58 and 39 in July and 33 in August. Consumers claim lenders refused or ignored ACH revocation requests, kept debiting after revocation, payoff, or account closure, or kept charging membership fees that were hard to cancel. These are unverified allegations.
brief.who_is_affected: Borrowers of payday, personal, and cash-advance products, including app-based advance and membership-model lenders, whose bank accounts are debited. Some claim overdraft or stop-payment fees as a result. Complaints are most common in TX and FL (13.1% each), followed by CA (6.9%). The AI-reviewed sample suggests 21.1% involve consumers flagged as potentially vulnerable, with mean severity of 3.87 out of 5.
brief.likely_root_cause: Hypothesis to test: some lenders may lack a reliable process to recognize and act on consumer requests to revoke debit authorization, particularly when a balance is outstanding or the request comes through customer service rather than a formal channel. Debit scheduling systems may not be synchronized with revocation, payoff, or account-closure status. Membership and subscription fee debits may be run on a separate billing system with hard-to-use cancellation paths. The sharp rise could also reflect a change at a few over-represented companies, since the lift concentration is high.
brief.process_or_control_to_check: Review ACH and recurring-payment authorization management: how revocation requests are received across channels, logged, and propagated to payment scheduling. Also review whether stop-payment and unlinking requests are honored, whether outstanding-balance conditions are applied to revocations, payoff and account-closure triggers that halt debits, membership cancellation and reactivation flows, and complaint escalation and root-cause tracking teams.
brief.regulatory_area: Electronic fund transfer authorization and revocation, including preauthorized recurring debits, plus consumer lending and subscription billing practices.
evidence: Recent monthly average of 43.33 complaints versus a baseline monthly average of 22.33.
June 2026 had 58 complaints, against baseline months ranging from 15 to 28.
Dave Operating, LLC has 62 complaints and a lift of 26.101.
Albert Corporation has 9 complaints and a lift of 15.844.
Bridge IT, Inc. has a lift of 6.455 and Self Financial Inc. has a lift of 5.052, each on small counts (2 and 3 complaints).
0.0% of the 36 narratives in recent months look templated.
In the AI sample of 38, 36.8% of narratives involve refusal to honor ACH revocation and 23.7% involve debits continuing after revocation or cancellation.
15.8% of the AI sample involve withdrawals after payoff or account closure and 10.5% involve membership or subscription fee withdrawals.
AI-assessed mean severity is 3.87 out of 5, and 21.1% of the sample involve potentially vulnerable consumers.
TX and FL each account for 13.1% of complaints.

checks.name: size
checks.reason: Dave Operating (62 complaints, lift 26.101) and Albert (9 complaints, lift 15.844) are far above lift 1, so the brief's company attribution is supported by lift rather than explained by market size.

checks.name: templating
checks.reason: 0.0% of the 36 recent narratives look templated, well under the 30% threshold.

checks.name: concentration
checks.reason: The top states are spread out (TX 13.1%, FL 13.1%, CA 6.9%) and complaints span many companies, so the signal is not confined to one state or one company.

checks.name: thin_evidence
checks.reason: The AI sample has 38 complaints and there are 36 recent narratives, and the revocation, continued-debit, payoff and membership themes cover roughly 87% of the sample (36.8%+23.7%+15.8%+10.5%), which supports the named root cause.

checks.name: seasonality
checks.reason: Monthly counts fell for the last two months (58 in June, 39 in July, 33 in August), leaving August about 43% below the peak and the 43.33 recent average propped up by June.

skeptic.note: Rejected because the surge peaked in June 2026 and has declined for two straight months, so the recent average overstates the current trend even though the other four checks passed.
